As we wrap up, I want you to remember—this isn’t just a story about the past. Racism, and the fight against it, is woven into the choices people make every single day. It’s in those tough questions we ask ourselves, and the courage it takes to not accept things that just aren’t fair. That journey toward a more just world? It’s long, sure. But it’s built out of small, everyday steps that anyone—yes, even you—can take.
So, what can you hold onto as you move forward?
First, every belief about race has a backstory. Take a moment to question where your own ideas come from. Second, don’t underestimate those small acts of resistance. They might seem tiny now, but they can grow into real change down the line. Third, listen—really listen—to other people’s stories. That’s how empathy grows, and how old assumptions finally get challenged.
Remember, it’s not enough to say you’re “not racist.” Real change means stepping up and confronting unfairness, even when it’s tough. And let’s be honest—progress is never a straight path. Setbacks will happen, but they’re just part of the journey, not the end.
Here’s the thing: you don’t need all the answers to make a difference. What matters most is your willingness to stay curious, keep learning, and take action—even when it feels uncomfortable. Change might start with noticing what’s wrong, but it grows when people come together, support each other, and refuse to give up hope.
You’re part of a long line of people who dared to dream of something better—and then rolled up their sleeves to make it real. This work isn’t easy, and it’s never really finished. But every step you take, every question you ask, every story you share, and every time you stand up for what’s right, you’re moving all of us a little closer to the world we want to see.
So, keep going. The future’s waiting for you.
